docs.title: tracemelt
docs.text:
Status: planned

tracemelt is at the design stage. This repository contains documentation tooling only. There is no collector config, query API, UI, alert engine or SDK to install yet. Applies to: dev (no release exists).

tracemelt is a planned open-source, OpenTelemetry-native observability platform for metrics, events, logs and traces (MELT). It is intended to be self-hostable and licensed under Apache-2.0.

docs.title: What exists today
docs.text:
Component Status Documentation site (MkDocs Material, mike, GitHub Pages) prototype OTLP ingest (OpenTelemetry Collector to ClickHouse) planned Query API planned Web UI planned Alert engine planned Node.js and Python SDKs planned Infrastructure metrics receivers planned

"Planned" means no code for it is in the repository.

docs.title: Intended design
docs.text:
These are design decisions, not working features:

  • OTLP is the only ingest contract. No proprietary telemetry protocol.
  • The OpenTelemetry Collector (contrib) receives OTLP on gRPC 4317 and HTTP 4318.
  • ClickHouse stores telemetry in tables owned by the collector's clickhouseexporter.
  • Events are structured logs tagged with tracemelt.event = "true", not a new signal.

docs.title: Where to go next
docs.text:
• Quickstart: what the first-run flow will be, and why it cannot be run yet.
  • Roadmap: phases, their acceptance criteria and current state.
  • Changelog: what has changed in this repository.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
Status: planned

This quickstart cannot be followed yet. The repository has no Docker Compose file and no services to start. Applies to: dev (no release exists).

This page will become a tutorial that takes a new user from a clean checkout to telemetry visible in the UI. Until the stack exists and the steps have been run end to end, it contains no commands, because any command here would fail.

docs.title: What the quickstart will cover
docs.text:
1. Start the single-node stack with Docker Compose.
  2. Check the health endpoint.
  3. Confirm demo traces, logs, metrics and events appear in the UI.
  4. Open a trace waterfall and follow a log to its trace.
  5. Create an alert and confirm a webhook delivery.

Each step will list the exact command, the expected output and a troubleshooting link.

docs.title: When this page changes status
docs.text: The banner moves to "prototype, verified on DATE" only after every step has been run on a clean machine and the outputs recorded here. See Phase 0 in the roadmap.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text:
Status: prototype

No version of tracemelt has been released. Entries below describe changes to this repository. Applies to: dev.

The format follows Keep a Changelog.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Apache-2.0 LICENSE and a README.
  • Roadmap and changelog pages.
  • Strict docs build as a gate before every docs deploy.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Project name in the docs is now tracemelt. The repository and docs URL remain observability-lens.
  • The landing page and quickstart are labelled "planned" and no longer describe components that are not in the repository.
  • Quickstart moved to getting-started/quickstart.md. The old /quickstart/ URL no longer resolves.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Broken link to a missing roadmap page, which made mkdocs build --strict fail.
  • Unclosed code block in the quickstart.
  • GitHub Pages 404: Pages now serves the gh-pages branch root and the site root redirects to dev.

docs.title: Roadmap
docs.text:
Status: planned

Everything below Phase -1 is planned work with no code in the repository. There are no dates. Applies to: dev (no release exists).

Phases are worked in order. A phase is complete only when its acceptance checks have been run and the results recorded.

docs.title: Phase -1: truth and docs live
docs.text:
State: in progress.

Check State Docs URL returns 200 done GitHub Pages serves the gh-pages branch root done mkdocs build --strict passes done Navigation references only existing files done Every page carries a status banner done /latest/ returns 200 not done: no release exists, the site root points at dev Remaining Wave 1 pages (MELT model, architecture, data model, ports, environment variables, alerting limitations, no-data troubleshooting) not done: they describe components that do not exist yet

docs.title: Phase 0: verify the quickstart
docs.text:
State: blocked. The collector config, ClickHouse setup, query API, UI, alert engine and demo workload have to be added to the repository before anything can be verified.

Acceptance: a new user can follow the quickstart without guessing, and every command has a recorded expected output.

docs.title: Phase 1: harden single-node
docs.text:
State: planned.

Scope: secrets from the environment, authenticated OTLP ingest, an authenticated UI and API, a persistent collector queue, query guardrails, webhook allowlisting with SSRF protection, self-metrics, disk and retention alerts, backup and restore, PII redaction defaults, fail-open SDK defaults.

docs.title: Phase 2: production shape
docs.text:
State: planned.

Scope: Postgres for rules, state, outbox and audit; OIDC and RBAC; separate ClickHouse users; alert resolution, silences, dedup and durable notification retries; histogram averages and real percentiles; per-series alerting; a Helm chart; upgrade documentation.

docs.title: Phase 3: scale and enterprise
docs.text:
State: planned.

Scope: highly available ClickHouse, collector gateway replicas, downsampling, tiered storage, multi-tenancy, quotas, tail sampling, cardinality controls and migration guides.
